report:
Reviewed the complete claim: (1) opening an associated signature must reuse owner Self and generic identities, (2) owner parameters precede associated-item parameters, (3) Binder pairs its value with binding parameters, and (4) copying/opening must not mint replacement identities. Ordinary implementation fns.rs opens the trait/impl signature through copy_into, copies its generic vector, takes trait Self from self_param or impl Self from self_ty, installs owner parameters before checking method generics, and appends method generics after the preserved owner prefix. None owners produce an empty owner prefix. ty.rs stores value and generics together, and Binder stash_copy copies both fields; captured Stashed::open returns the existing root, copy_into delegates to stash_copy, slice copying preserves elements through StashCopy, and GenericParam is StashDirect so the copied symbols are unchanged. CheckGenerics creates only the item's own parameters with the item's parent identity. These are source-inspection findings, not blanket test coverage claims.

All four test entries were inspected. associated_items_reuse_owner_generics_and_bodies_resolve_fields checks an impl method has one owner generic, a receiver whose Wrap argument equals the return type, and a successfully checked field-access body. trait_and_impl_signatures_share_complete_generic_binders checks trait Self-plus-T binder size, impl T binder size, and identical tuple-element types. trait_items_have_stable_symbols_and_owner_identity checks the trait method's entire generic slice equals the owning trait-items binder and checks associated item owners; it also distinguishes receiverless associated functions. These substantively cover trait Self identity and impl parameter reuse, but do not establish arbitrary copy/open identity or simultaneous owner-plus-method parameter ordering. The existing explicit TODO test types_binder_owner_parameters accurately preserves those missing cases and all-item-kind coverage; it is a placeholder and is not counted as execution evidence. Its all-kind coverage requires checked alias/constant signatures, which do not yet exist in the captured symbol implementations. The new implementation TODO in ty::todo makes that missing behavior explicit: aliases and constants currently have owner identity/CST/attributes, and need checked signature APIs that open owner binders before item parameters. This is a justified implementation deferral, not a declaration that all associated signatures are implemented. The Binder and function implementation associations remain ordinary.

Executed cargo fmt, cargo build (passed with existing warnings), and cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib trait_system_tests::trait_items_have_stable_symbols_and_owner_identity -- --exact (one passed). The other two substantive tests were source-reviewed rather than executed in this assignment. Added only an ordinary Binder association and the precise TODO implementation explanation in ty.rs; no semantic implementation changes. Central post-codegen and Sage-sanity reviews are coordinated by root. No further edits requested for this truthful mixture of implemented evidence and explicit deferred coverage.
